action: The PIPC has set out 20 security measures for public agencies and companies to implement first; follow the PIPC's list and its December-to-February inspection support.
date_note: Digital Daily's articles of 27 November say the PIPC announced the response on the 27th.
exec: South Korea's PIPC reports 1,019 breach reports from January to October and will run inspection support from December for three months.
geo_basis: Agency is South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission; pin placed at Seoul as the national capital, no address stated in the sources
plain: South Korea's privacy regulator says breach reports are far above last year's level, so from December it will give public bodies and companies three months of inspection support.
summary: Digital Daily reports that South Korea's Personal Information Protection Commission announced on 27 November an emergency response and inspection support system. January to October 2026 saw 1,019 breach reports, 271 public and 748 private, against 447 in all of last year. The PIPC expects the yearly total to exceed three times last year's, and plans three months of inspection support from December.
title: South Korea's PIPC activates emergency response as breach reports reach 1,019 in January to October, over double all of 2025

validation.note: Two Digital Daily articles (one publisher) relay the PIPC's 27 November announcement; no PIPC release or second publisher was read.

evidence.quote: 올해 1월부터 10월까지 접수된 개인정보 유출신고는 총 1019건으로 지난해 전체 유출신고 건수인 447건의 2배를 넘어섰다.
개인정보위는 공공기관과 민간기업이 우선 이행해야 할 20개 보안조치 사항도 마련했다.
개인정보위는 올해 개인정보 유출사고 신고 건수가 지난해의 3배를 넘어설 것으로 전망했다.
